title: Review 2
description: Word order, present tense, negation, infinitives, and numbers
descriptionRussian: Порядок слов, настоящее время, отрицание, инфинитив и числа
intro: This review covers Russian word order (flexible but with common patterns), present tense conjugation for regular and irregular verbs, negation with не, verb infinitives, and numbers 1-100. These building blocks let you form statements, deny things, and count.
rules: Russian word order is flexible, but the most common pattern is Subject-Verb-Object: Я читаю книгу.
Present tense verbs have two conjugation patterns: -е- (1st) and -и- (2nd). Я читаю, ты читаешь vs. я говорю, ты говоришь.
Negation uses не before the verb: Я не говорю по-русски. (I don't speak Russian.)
The infinitive is the base form ending in -ть: читать (to read), говорить (to speak), писать (to write).
Numbers: один (1), два (2), три (3), десять (10), двадцать (20), сто (100). After 2-4, use genitive singular.
examples: Я читаю книгу. (I read a book.) — Subject + Verb + Object
Она не работает сегодня. (She doesn't work today.) — не before the verb
Я хочу читать. (I want to read.) — infinitive after хочу
У меня двадцать пять рублей. (I have twenty-five rubles.)

items.prompt: Choose the correct form: Я _____ книгу. (read)
items.explanation: With я, the verb takes -ю/-у ending: я читаю.

items.prompt: Choose the correct form: Они _____ по-русски. (speak)
items.explanation: With они, 2nd conjugation verbs take -ят: они говорят.

items.prompt: How do you say 'I don't understand'?
items.hint: Не goes directly before the verb
items.explanation: Negation in Russian uses не placed directly before the verb: Я не понимаю.

items.promptEnglish: Which is the infinitive (base) form of the verb?
items.explanation: The infinitive is the base form of the verb, ending in -ть: читать (to read).
Пятнадцать (15) = пять (5) + надцать (teen suffix). Numbers 11-19 follow this pattern.

items.prompt: Choose the correct form: Ты _____ музыку. (listen to)
items.explanation: With ты, 1st conjugation verbs take -ешь: ты слушаешь.

items.prompt: Which sentence has correct word order?
items.promptEnglish: Which sentence correctly says 'Anna reads a book'?
items.hint: The most neutral order is Subject-Verb-Object
items.explanation: While all options are technically grammatical, Анна читает книгу (SVO) is the most neutral, common word order.
Пятьдесят (50) = пять (5) + десят (tens). Tens 50-80 follow this compound pattern.

sentenceBuilding.translation: She wants to read a book.

minimalPairs.explanation: Читаю is the conjugated present tense (I read). Читать is the infinitive (to read).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I want to read a book.
minimalPairs.explanation: After хочу (want), use the infinitive: читать (to read).
Не is used before verbs for negation. Нет means 'no' as a standalone answer.

minimalPairs.context: Ты говоришь по-русски? — _____, я не говорю.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Do you speak Russian? No, I don't speak it.
minimalPairs.explanation: Нет is used as a standalone 'no'. Не is used before verbs.
